data.name: Ayayra
data.gender_notes: Ayayra is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'ayyara', meaning 'to shine', 'to be radiant'. Ayayra refers to the light of the moon. The name Ayayra carries the meaning “Moonlight, radiant light” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ayayra usually hope their child will grow to embody moonlight, radiant light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Inspires inner peace and tranquility, and brings a sense of spiritual connection to the natural world.
data.etymology: Ayayra belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moonlight, radiant light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayayra total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_arabic.name: آيراء
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مؤنث مشتق من الأسماء التي تعبر عن الجمال والرقة
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم آيراء هو اسم علم مؤنث من أصل عربي، مشتق من الأسماء التي تعبر عن الجمال والرقة. يتميز بالجمال والسلاسة في النطق، ويحمل معاني جميلة تتعلق بالطبيعة والإنسانية. وقد وردت الأسماء المشتقة من نفس الجذر في القرآن الكريم، مما يعطيها قيمة دينية وروحية كبيرة.

in_urdu.name: آیرا
in_urdu.meaning: ایک خوبصورت اور نازک نام، جو اسلامی روایات میں جمال و خوبی کی علامت ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: آیرا ایک علم نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے خوبصورت، نازک اور ملائم۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی روایات میں بہت مقبول ہے، خاص طور پر پاکستان اور بھارت میں۔ اس کا تعلق اسلامی ثقافت اور تاریخ سے ہے، اور یہ اکثر خوبصورت اور پاکیزہ معنوں کے ساتھ جڑا ہوا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: आइरा
in_hindi.meaning: एक सुंदर और कोमल नाम, जो इस्लामी परंपराओं में सौंदर्य और शालीनता का प्रतीक है
in_hindi.long_meaning: आइरा एक सुंदर और अर्थपूर्ण नाम है जो अरबी मूल से लिया गया है। इसका अर्थ है 'सुंदर', 'कोमल', और 'शालीन'। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में बहुत लोकप्रिय है और अक्सर इसकी सुंदरता और पवित्रता के अर्थों के साथ जुड़ा होता है। यह नाम इस्लामी संस्कृति और परंपराओं में गहरा महत्व रखता है।

in_pashto.name: آيره
in_pashto.meaning: د ښکلا او نرموالي سمبول، په افغان او پښتون کلتور کې مهموالی
in_pashto.long_meaning: آيره د ښکلا او نرموالي نښه ده. دا نوم په پښتو او افغان کلتور کې ډیر مشهور دی او د ښکلا، پاکيزۍ او روحانيت معنی لري. دا نوم د پښتون او افغان ټولنو کې د ښځو لپاره کارول کیږي او ډیر ستر ارزښت لري.

in_english.name: Ayayra
in_english.meaning: Beautiful, delicate, and elegant name with Arabic origins
in_english.long_meaning: Ayayra is a feminine given name of Arabic origin, meaning 'beautiful', 'delicate', and 'elegant'. It is derived from Arabic roots that signify beauty, refinement, and spirituality. Although not directly mentioned in the Quran, names with similar roots are highly regarded in Islamic tradition for their positive connotations. Ayayra symbolizes qualities such as kindness, purity, and charm, making it a popular choice among Muslim parents worldwide. The name reflects a rich cultural heritage and carries a sense of serenity and grace.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ayayra has a rich cultural significance in Islamic tradition, particularly during the holy month of Ramadan when Muslims around the world fast from dawn till sunset. Ayayra is the name of the star Aljubbah, which began to appear after the break of the fast, heralding the arrival of the beloved month. Every day, as the sun sets and the first star of Shawwal appears, excited children and worshippers alike gather to celebrate the end of the day's fast. Families and communities come together as the collective sound of the 'adhan' (call to prayer) echoes through the streets, reminding everyone of the communal worship, unity, and love within the Islamic community.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ayayra holds a profound spiritual significance with its reference to the moon's light. In Islamic tradition, the light of the moon and the sun are symbols of divine guidance for the believers. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) said, "There is no light for the believer in this world but the light of Allah, and there is no darkness for him but the darkness of his own misdeeds" [Bukhari]. This teaches us to strive for a constant connection with Allah, and to seek out His light during times of hardship and darkness in our lives. In the context of Ayayra, the shining of the star serves as a reminder for Muslims to seek and live in the light of Allah's wisdom and guidance.
